analogy.name: Opening a restaurant for the day
analogy.line: The landlord unlocks the building (firmware), the manager picks the plan (GRUB), staff arrive (kernel), jobs are handed out (systemd), the host seats you (login).

analogy.name: A festival wristband
analogy.line: Show ID once at the gate (the domain controller), get a wristband (Kerberos ticket), then every stage lets you in by the wristband without asking for ID again.

analogy.name: Posting a letter
analogy.line: The letter (data) goes in an envelope with a street address (IP), a flat number picks who reads it (port), and the post office only cares about the envelope, not the letter.

analogy.name: Supermarket checkout lanes
analogy.line: One person waves you to an open till. A closed till (failed health check) gets no customers, and you never need to know which till you used.

analogy.name: A shipping container
analogy.line: Same sealed box on a ship, a train or a truck. The image is the packed container, a container is one of them actually in transit.

analogy.name: An air traffic control tower
analogy.line: The tower (control plane) decides where each plane goes, ground crew at each gate (kubelet) handle it, and the gate number (Service) stays the same whichever plane is parked there.

analogy.name: A car dashboard
analogy.line: Sensors in the engine (instrumentation) feed the gauges (metrics), a warning light comes on at a threshold (alert), and someone has to pull over (respond).

analogy.name: A doctor's diagnosis
analogy.line: Reproduce the symptom, rule things out one at a time, form one theory, treat it, then check the patient is actually better.

analogy.name: Undo history vs a copy in a safe
analogy.line: A snapshot is undo history on the same disk: lose the disk, lose it. A backup is a copy kept somewhere else.

analogy.name: Badge doors in a hospital
analogy.line: Getting through the front entrance does not open every ward. Each door checks your badge again, which is zero trust.
